title: Basic Beet Pickle
subtitle: Recipe Formulation Sheet

meta.baseTargetScale: 1 quart jar / 450 g raw beet base

summary: A deliberately minimal quick pickle built on a 1:1 water-to-rice-wine-vinegar ratio. Character is clean, crisp, and mineral-forward.

The restraint is the point. With no dill, ginger, or warming spice, this pickle does not compete with anything else in the container — it stays a structural element next to assertive neighbors like kimchi or a dark miso dressing. Rice wine vinegar is also gentler than apple cider vinegar, which keeps the beets firm and snappy across a full week rather than going floppy by midweek.

specs.label: Cure Time
specs.value: Cool to room temp, then refrigerate

scalingPrinciple: Item A.01 (Raw Beets) is locked at 100.0% as the substrate baseline. The brine components read against that beet mass — critically, water and vinegar stay locked to each other at 1:1 regardless of batch size, since that ratio is what buffers the acidity enough to preserve texture.

rows.name: Raw Beets, cut into matchsticks
rows.role: Primary substrate; a source of betaine. Cut to matchsticks for maximum brine surface contact.

rows.name: Rice Wine Vinegar
rows.role: Gentle acid — less aggressive than cider vinegar, which is what preserves the snap.

rows.name: Water
rows.role: Buffers acidity to keep the beets firm rather than slack.

rows.name: Garlic, smashed
rows.role: The only aromatic in the formulation — sulfur compounds, kept deliberately singular.

matrixFootnote: *This formulation is given in volumetric kitchen units and counts in the source. All gram values are standard culinary conversions and are marked accordingly; none are source-stated weights.

mise.label: Prep (A.01, C.01)
mise.text: Cut the raw beets into matchsticks. Smash the garlic cloves. Pack both into your jar.

execution.name: Brine
execution.text: Simmer the rice wine vinegar, water, and salt just until the salt dissolves — no longer. This is a dissolution step, not a reduction.

execution.name: Combine
execution.text: Pour the hot liquid over the packed beets and garlic.

execution.name: Cure
execution.params: To room temp, then cold | Refrigerated
execution.text: Let cool on the counter, then refrigerate.

sections.title: Serving Notes
sections.intro: Built as a component rather than a standalone condiment:

items.label: The mix:
items.text: Rice or quinoa base, plus carrots, plus the pickled beets.

items.label: The sauce:
items.text: Garlic-tahini, made with dark black miso and a splash of the rice wine vinegar from the pickle jar.

items.label: Why it stays plain:
items.text: Without herbs like dill or ginger, the pickle won't compete with a bok choy kimchi or a dark miso dressing sharing the same bowl. It stays in its lane as a structural, acidic element.

directive: Simmer the brine only until the salt dissolves. Boiling it down concentrates the acid past the 1:1 ratio the formulation depends on, and over-acidified brine is what turns matchsticks floppy within a couple of days.
